candidates.attacker_control: The party supplying the specification document controls the `$ref` strings (definitions, properties, paths, parameters, responses) parsed by `SwaggerDeserializer` (e.g. SwaggerDeserializer.java:1017-1022) and, for legacy 1.x documents, the `apis[].path`/`basePath` values. These strings become the URL/path operands of the loaders above. For the credential-disclosure aspect the attacker chooses a `$ref` host while the application passes its own `AuthorizationValue` list (the usage pattern shown in README.md lines 44-62).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Fetching external references is a documented/implemented feature (ResolverCache class comment, ExternalRefProcessor, README), so this is a trust-boundary issue that matters when the document source is untrusted; the library offers no flag to disable resolution in the reviewed API. For the local-read branch the loaded content must deserialize as the expected type or the load throws (ResolverCache.java:120-144; DeserializationUtils.java:22-24, 48-50), limiting direct exfiltration to parseable files. The legacy 1.1 `basePath` path does validate scheme/host via `checkLegalBasePath` and `LEGAL_SCHEMES` (V11ResourceListingMigrator.java:29-74), showing one path partly hardened while the 2.0 `$ref` and 1.2 `apis[].path` paths are not; this is noted as partial mitigation, not full coverage. `file:`-scheme refs may be classified RELATIVE by the dependency and then fail path resolution rather than read a file, so the arbitrary-read claim is limited to absolute/`..` paths (and http(s)/ftp refs for SSRF). Behavior was not executed.
candidates.impact: Server-side request forgery from the parsing process against internal/loopback/cloud-metadata endpoints; disclosure of caller-supplied API keys/tokens (header or query `AuthorizationValue`s) to an attacker-selected host named in a `$ref`; and, when parsing a local document, read of files outside the specification's directory (absolute paths or `../` escapes) whose contents can then surface in the resolved model if they parse as JSON/YAML.
candidates.prerequisites: An application uses `SwaggerParser.read(...)`/`readWithInfo(...)` (external resolution is on by default: SwaggerParser.java:67, 35) or `SwaggerCompatConverter.read(...)` on a document whose content is not fully trusted. For credential disclosure, the caller passes plain `AuthorizationValue`s rather than `HostAuthorizationValue` (the opt-in host-scoped wrapper exists at util/HostAuthorizationValue.java). For local file reads, the root location must be a local path so `parentDirectory` is set (ResolverCache.java:64-73).
candidates.root_cause: Spec content is trusted for resource locations. `$ref` strings (and legacy resource-listing paths) are split/joined and passed directly to network/file loaders with no protocol, host, or directory-containment validation: `ResolverCache.loadRef` (ResolverCache.java:110-118) hands the attacker-supplied file/URL portion to `RefUtils.readExternalRef`/`readExternalUrlRef`; the URL branch calls `RemoteUrl.urlToString` (RefUtils.java:59, 127), which does `new URL(cleanUrl(url))` and `openConnection()` for any JDK-supported scheme/host (RemoteUrl.java:98, 124, 133); the relative branch does `parentDirectory.resolve(file).normalize()` (RefUtils.java:130) with no check that the result stays under `parentDirectory`, so absolute paths and `../` escapes are read via FileInputStream (RefUtils.java:133) or the classpath (RefUtils.java:135). Additionally, when the root location is remote, `ResolverCache` passes `parentDirectory == null` (ResolverCache.java:64-73) and relative URLs are rebuilt and fetched (RefUtils.java:74-114). `RemoteUrl.urlToString` then applies every plain (non-`ManagedValue`) `AuthorizationValue` as a header or query parameter to whatever URL is being fetched (RemoteUrl.java:101-109, 127-129), i.e. to attacker-selected hosts as well. The legacy converter repeats the pattern: `SwaggerCompatConverter.read` builds a fetch location from the attacker-controlled `ApiListingReference.getPath()` (SwaggerCompatConverter.java:135-169) and `readDeclaration` fetches it via `RemoteUrl.urlToString` (SwaggerCompatConverter.java:487).
candidates.title: Unvalidated external-reference resolution: SSRF, local file read, and credential disclosure to attacker-chosen URLs
candidates.trace: spec text/file -> Swagger20Parser/SwaggerDeserializer -> Swagger -> SwaggerResolver.resolve() -> DefinitionsProcessor/ModelProcessor/PropertyProcessor/PathsProcessor/OperationProcessor/ParameterProcessor -> ResolverCache.loadRef(ref, refFormat, ...) -> RefUtils.readExternalRef / readExternalUrlRef -> RemoteUrl.urlToString (new URL(...).openConnection(), credentials attached to arbitrary host) or parentDirectory.resolve(ref).normalize() + FileInputStream / ClasspathHelper; legacy path: SwaggerCompatConverter.read -> ref.getPath() -> readDeclaration -> RemoteUrl.urlToString.
candidates.unverified: Exact `RefFormat` assignment for non-http schemes is computed inside the swagger-models dependency (not present in the snapshot), so the precise scheme set that reaches the URL branch is inferred from `RefUtils.isAnExternalRefFormat`/`ExternalRefProcessor` usage rather than verified; runtime reachability, server-side parsing of untrusted specs, and actual responses were not tested; test sources are not part of the snapshot.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-918 SSRF (also CWE-22 local file read and CWE-522 credential exposure)

coverage_summary: Scope: 141 model-visible files, all listed as source-root files (0 excluded by sensitive-name/symlink/binary filters; binary-like files are refused on read). Reviewed both modules' Java sources (swagger-parser: parser, resolver, processors, util classes, 63KB SwaggerDeserializer mostly skimmed; swagger-compat-spec-parser: converter, legacy reader/deserializer/validate/migrate paths) and the pom.xml dependency/version declarations. The P1 relation index reports 141/141 files indexed, 0 hash mismatches/missing files, 824 symbols, 1438 edges, 2858 calls and only 7 navigation facts (3 pom config facts and 3 network/sql name-based `security_call` hints, incl. RemoteUrl.java:121-124); no data-flow, reachability, or exploitability claims follow from it. Test sources and META-INF service descriptors are absent from the snapshot, so parser-extension wiring and test-verified behavior could not be inspected.
limitations: No build, tests, scanners, or runtime execution were performed; all conclusions are static source reading.
The `RefFormat` enum and swagger-core model classes live in a dependency not present in the snapshot, so attacker ref-to-format mapping and exact loader branch are inferred, not proven.
Transitive dependency versions (SnakeYAML via swagger-core 1.5.15; Apache HttpClient in the compat module) are not pinned in the snapshot, limiting verification of the YAML and HTTP-client leads.
Test sources, META-INF service registrations, and any files outside the 141-file filtered view were not available, so data-flow and reachability statements are limited to the visible code.
The relation index is syntax-level only; it cannot confirm data flow, runtime behavior, or which of the several plausible leads the case concerns.

rejected_leads.lead: Unsafe SnakeYAML default constructor when parsing untrusted YAML specs: `DeserializationUtils.readYamlTree` and `readYamlValue` instantiate `new org.yaml.snakeyaml.Yaml()` and call `load()` (modules/swagger-parser/src/main/java/io/swagger/parser/util/DeserializationUtils.java:59-67), reachable from public entry points SwaggerParser.readWithInfo(String) (SwaggerParser.java:99), Swagger20Parser.readWithInfo/convertToSwagger (Swagger20Parser.java:64, 121) and external-ref content (DeserializationUtils.java:20).
rejected_leads.reason: Strong CWE-502 pattern, but its exploitability rests on the transitive SnakeYAML version's default `Constructor` semantics; SnakeYAML is not in the snapshot and no version is pinned (only swagger-core 1.5.15 at pom.xml:239), so the unsafe behavior could not be verified from source text alone. Kept as a follow-up lead rather than the single submitted candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Trust-all TLS configuration (RemoteUrl.java:34-79, `io.swagger.parser.util.RemoteUrl.trustAll` system property disables certificate and hostname validation).
rejected_leads.reason: Opt-in, operator-set configuration rather than attacker-controlled input; no attacker path shown.

rejected_leads.lead: Unbounded/recursive external-ref resolution (ExternalRefProcessor.processRefToExternalDefinition/processRefProperty, ExternalRefProcessor.java:33-121) permitting cyclic external refs and stack exhaustion.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible DoS, but impact and reachability are weaker/more speculative than the submitted candidate and it shares the same external-ref root cause.

summary: Reviewed the 141-file swagger-parser snapshot (modules/swagger-parser and modules/swagger-compat-spec-parser main sources plus bundled resources). The strongest source-evidenced issue is the unvalidated dereferencing of attacker-controlled external references during spec parsing: `$ref` values (and legacy 1.x `apis[].path`) taken from the parsed document drive `ResolverCache`/`RefUtils`/`RemoteUrl`/`SwaggerCompatConverter` to fetch arbitrary URLs or read arbitrary local paths, with no scheme/host/path allowlist, and caller-supplied `AuthorizationValue` credentials are attached to every fetched URL. I submit that as one candidate (SSRF + local file read + credential disclosure). The unsafe SnakeYAML default-constructor usage in `DeserializationUtils` is noted as a strong but unverifiable-in-snapshot secondary lead.
